question: Should OpenClaw accept `tools.fs.workspaceAliases` as a standalone host-mode filesystem escape hatch for exact workspace symlink aliases?
rationale: The PR adds a public config surface and changes a security-sensitive workspace boundary while related open PRs propose broader filesystem-root and PathGuard models.

options.title: Approve Exact Alias Contract
options.body: Accept the narrow exact-realpath alias design, host-only scope, and plugin-policy exposure after security review, then merge once maintainers are satisfied.

options.title: Fold Into Broader FS Policy
options.body: Pause this PR and route the memory-alias case into a broader `tools.fs.roots` or PathGuard direction if maintainers want one filesystem policy surface.

options.title: Narrow To Memory-Owned Config
options.body: Revise the PR to a memory-specific root or doctor/status flow if aliases should not become a general file-tool config contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Exact Alias Contract
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow exact-realpath alias design, host-only scope, and plugin-policy exposure after security review, then merge once maintainers are satisfied.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history and prior-review signal around the existing workspace-only filesystem policy and security-sensitive config framing.
